title: Too Many Young Men Don’t Know How to Be a Gentleman
gist: Leonard Sax uses the Cornell Chi Phi sexual-assault lawsuit to argue that adults have stopped teaching boys basic norms such as not taking advantage of intoxicated women, while pervasive and increasingly violent pornography fills the gap. He links this to young women's growing 'heteropessimism', citing a survey in which only 36% of single women aged 18-29 said they were interested in dating a man.

insights.claim: A woman who alleges she was sexually assaulted by seven men at Cornell University's Chi Phi fraternity in October 2024 filed suit on September 16, 2026, against the men, the fraternity, her sorority and the university.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Universities face growing legal and reputational liability over Greek-life incidents.

insights.claim: Leonard Sax argues that boys must be taught with authority to govern themselves and channel sexual desire into romance rather than violence, but many school leaders and parents are now uncomfortable even with the word 'gentleman.'
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: This points to a possible cultural and educational push around raising boys, part of the wider debate about young men.
insights.quote: For a boy to become a good man, he must be taught how to govern himself—how to channel his sexual desire into romance rather than into violence.
